quests.hint: A word that steers the conversation to a new or main topic.
quests.explanation: 'So, anyway' is a natural spoken way to change the topic or return to the main point. It is informal.
quests.textToSpeak: Enough about my holiday. So, ___, how's the new job going?
quests.correctAnswer: Enough about my holiday. So, anyway, how's the new job going?
quests.contextClue: 'Enough about my holiday' signals a change of topic.

quests.hint: A noun in the fixed phrase that introduces a side topic.
quests.explanation: 'By the way' introduces a side topic or afterthought: 'By the way, did you...?'
quests.textToSpeak: By the ___, have you heard from Sam about Saturday?
quests.correctAnswer: By the way, have you heard from Sam about Saturday?
quests.contextClue: A side question is added to the conversation.

quests.hint: A discourse word that introduces something unexpected.
quests.explanation: 'Actually' can introduce a surprising fact or a correction. Here it shows the real feeling differed from the expectation.
quests.textToSpeak: I thought the film would be boring, but ___, I really enjoyed it.
quests.correctAnswer: I thought the film would be boring, but actually, I really enjoyed it.
quests.contextClue: 'Thought... but' contrasts expectation with reality.

quests.hint: A verb for asking yourself a question.
quests.explanation: 'I wonder if' expresses curiosity or uncertainty. It is a natural way to think aloud.
quests.textToSpeak: I ___ if the shop is still open; it's nearly nine.
quests.correctAnswer: I wonder if the shop is still open; it's nearly nine.
quests.contextClue: The speaker isn't sure and is thinking aloud.

quests.hint: Make the effort to do something.
quests.explanation: 'Don't bother' + -ing tells someone the effort is unnecessary: 'don't bother waiting'. 'Bother' can also mean disturb.
quests.textToSpeak: Don't ___ waiting for me; I might be late.
quests.correctAnswer: Don't bother waiting for me; I might be late.
quests.contextClue: Possible lateness makes waiting unnecessary.

quests.hint: Talk about something briefly.
quests.explanation: 'Don't mention it' is a polite reply to thanks. It means 'you're welcome'.
quests.textToSpeak: You don't need to thank me. Really, don't ___ it.
quests.correctAnswer: You don't need to thank me. Really, don't mention it.
quests.contextClue: A reply that plays down thanks.

quests.hint: The good feeling when a worry ends.
quests.explanation: 'What a relief!' expresses the good feeling when a worry ends. 'What a + noun!' is a common way to react.
quests.textToSpeak: I've finally finished all my exams. What a ___!
quests.correctAnswer: I've finally finished all my exams. What a relief!
quests.contextClue: Finishing exams ends a stressful period.

quests.hint: A verb for how something seems when you hear about it.
quests.explanation: 'That sounds + adjective' reacts to news or a plan: 'That sounds great', 'That sounds difficult'.
quests.textToSpeak: A picnic by the river on Sunday? That ___ great to me.
quests.correctAnswer: A picnic by the river on Sunday? That sounds great to me.
quests.contextClue: The speaker is reacting to a plan just heard.

quests.hint: The parts of your head you hear with.
quests.explanation: 'I'm all ears' means you are ready to listen carefully.
quests.textToSpeak: Go on, tell me what happened. I'm all ___.
quests.correctAnswer: Go on, tell me what happened. I'm all ears.
quests.contextClue: A request to tell a story invites listening.

quests.hint: An adjective describing a caring person.
quests.explanation: 'Would you be so kind as to...' is a very polite, formal request. It is more formal than 'Could you...?'
quests.textToSpeak: Would you be so ___ as to close the window? It's freezing in here.
quests.correctAnswer: Would you be so kind as to close the window? It's freezing in here.
quests.contextClue: The politeness level is very high.

quests.hint: Pause before acting because you're unsure.
quests.explanation: 'Don't hesitate to + verb' is a polite way to invite someone to get in touch.
quests.textToSpeak: Please don't ___ to call me if you have any questions.
quests.correctAnswer: Please don't hesitate to call me if you have any questions.
quests.contextClue: Messages often end with this invitation.

quests.hint: A feeling of enjoyment and satisfaction.
quests.explanation: 'My pleasure' is a warm reply to thanks. It is a little warmer than 'You're welcome'.
quests.textToSpeak: Honestly, it was my ___; I was going past your house.
quests.correctAnswer: Honestly, it was my pleasure; I was going past your house.
quests.contextClue: A friendly reply to being thanked.

quests.hint: Risk money on the outcome of something.
quests.explanation: 'Bet' means wager money. In speech, 'I bet' also means 'I'm sure'. It is irregular: bet, bet, bet.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll ___ you five pounds that he forgets his ticket again.
quests.correctAnswer: I'll bet you five pounds that he forgets his ticket again.
quests.contextClue: Money is offered on a prediction.

quests.hint: Have a debt to someone.
quests.explanation: 'I owe you one' means I'll return the favour someday. 'Owe' is also used for money.
quests.textToSpeak: Thanks for covering my shift, Priya. I ___ you one.
quests.correctAnswer: Thanks for covering my shift, Priya. I owe you one.
quests.contextClue: The speaker was helped at work.

quests.hint: Something you pay for as a nice gesture.
quests.explanation: 'My treat' means I'm paying. 'Treat' can also mean behave toward someone or give medical care.
quests.textToSpeak: Put your wallet away. Dinner is my ___ tonight.
quests.correctAnswer: Put your wallet away. Dinner is my treat tonight.
quests.contextClue: Putting the wallet away signals that someone else pays.

quests.hint: In some place, not yet named.
quests.explanation: With 'somewhere', 'something' and 'anything', the adjective comes after: 'somewhere quiet', 'something new'.
quests.textToSpeak: Let's go ___ quiet where we can talk properly.
quests.correctAnswer: Let's go somewhere quiet where we can talk properly.
quests.contextClue: A private talk needs a certain kind of place.

quests.hint: Any single thing, used in negatives.
quests.explanation: Use 'anything' in negatives and questions: 'I haven't got anything smaller'. In positive sentences we use 'something'.
quests.textToSpeak: Sorry, I haven't got ___ smaller than a twenty-pound note.
quests.correctAnswer: Sorry, I haven't got anything smaller than a twenty-pound note.
quests.contextClue: 'Haven't got' triggers the negative form.

quests.hint: A thing that isn't named.
quests.explanation: 'Something' is used in positive sentences: 'I've got something to tell you'. In negatives we use 'anything'.
quests.textToSpeak: I've got ___ to tell you, but you have to promise not to laugh.
quests.correctAnswer: I've got something to tell you, but you have to promise not to laugh.
quests.contextClue: A secret is about to be shared.

quests.hint: An adverb meaning precisely.
quests.explanation: 'That's exactly what I meant' emphasises that something matches perfectly.
quests.textToSpeak: Yes, that's ___ what I meant! You explained it better than I did.
quests.correctAnswer: Yes, that's exactly what I meant! You explained it better than I did.
quests.contextClue: The speaker's meaning was captured perfectly.

quests.hint: An adverb used when you've heard something but haven't seen it yourself.
quests.explanation: 'Apparently' reports something you have heard but not confirmed.
quests.textToSpeak: I haven't seen it myself, but, ___, the train service has stopped for the day.
quests.correctAnswer: I haven't seen it myself, but, apparently, the train service has stopped for the day.
quests.contextClue: 'I haven't seen it myself' shows the information is secondhand.

quests.hint: An adverb showing you expect the listener to agree.
quests.explanation: 'Surely' expresses that you find it hard to believe otherwise: 'Surely you've heard of him?'
quests.textToSpeak: You've ___ heard of him; he's on TV every night.
quests.correctAnswer: You've surely heard of him; he's on TV every night.
quests.contextClue: TV fame makes not knowing surprising.

quests.hint: A British informal verb meaning to want to do something.
quests.explanation: 'Do you fancy + -ing?' is a friendly British way to suggest an activity.
quests.textToSpeak: Do you ___ going for a walk after lunch? The sun has come out.
quests.correctAnswer: Do you fancy going for a walk after lunch? The sun has come out.
quests.contextClue: The sun coming out is a reason to suggest a walk.

quests.hint: Unable to leave a place or situation.
quests.explanation: 'Stuck at home' means unable to go out. Also: 'stuck in traffic', 'stuck on a problem'.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd love to come, but I'm ___ at home with a stomach bug.
quests.correctAnswer: I'd love to come, but I'm stuck at home with a stomach bug.
quests.contextClue: Illness prevents the speaker from attending.

quests.hint: Meaning or logic.
quests.explanation: 'That makes sense' means I understand the logic. 'That doesn't make sense' expresses confusion.
quests.textToSpeak: Oh, now that makes ___! I couldn't understand why she was upset.
quests.correctAnswer: Oh, now that makes sense! I couldn't understand why she was upset.
quests.contextClue: The speaker suddenly understands a puzzling situation.

quests.hint: The noun in the phrase meaning to briefly get in contact.
quests.explanation: 'Touch base' means briefly contact someone to update them. It is common in workplace speech.
quests.textToSpeak: Let's touch ___ next week to see how the project is going.
quests.correctAnswer: Let's touch base next week to see how the project is going.
quests.contextClue: A follow-up next week is planned to check progress.

quests.hint: A ring shape; in this phrase it is about being informed.
quests.explanation: 'Keep me in the loop' means keep me informed. 'In the loop' means you are included in the information.
quests.textToSpeak: Please keep me in the ___ about any changes to the plan.
quests.correctAnswer: Please keep me in the loop about any changes to the plan.
quests.contextClue: Changes need to be communicated to the speaker.

quests.hint: One side of a sheet in a book.
quests.explanation: 'On the same page' means sharing the same understanding. It is common in work conversations.
quests.textToSpeak: Let's make sure we're all on the same ___ before we talk to the client.
quests.correctAnswer: Let's make sure we're all on the same page before we talk to the client.
quests.contextClue: Before meeting the client, the team must agree.

quests.hint: The opposite of long.
quests.explanation: 'To cut a long story short' means to summarise quickly. American speakers often say 'to make a long story short'.
quests.textToSpeak: To cut a long story ___, we missed the flight and stayed overnight in Frankfurt.
quests.correctAnswer: To cut a long story short, we missed the flight and stayed overnight in Frankfurt.
quests.contextClue: A summary is about to follow.

quests.hint: The value of something.
quests.explanation: 'For what it's worth' introduces an opinion you offer modestly, without pushing it.
quests.textToSpeak: For what it's ___, I think you made the right choice.
quests.correctAnswer: For what it's worth, I think you made the right choice.
quests.contextClue: The speaker is offering an opinion modestly.

quests.hint: Involved or affected.
quests.explanation: 'As far as I'm concerned' introduces your personal position or view.
quests.textToSpeak: As far as I'm ___, the matter is closed and we can move on.
quests.correctAnswer: As far as I'm concerned, the matter is closed and we can move on.
quests.contextClue: The speaker states their own view that the matter is finished.
